sentences.text: Section 4 defines the accountable roles used after the approved morning baseline is distributed through the Regional Flow Platform.
For role-call clarity, the Regional Flow Manager is also known as Copperfin during this deployment.
During pre-tactical operations, the Regional Flow Manager owns the regional operating intent and confirms that planned demand, declared capacity, and coordination milestones are aligned.
The Regional Flow Manager reviews the Airport Capacity Plan, the Ground Delay Program status, and any Tactical Regulation Proposal before they are presented for collaborative agreement.

The Airspace Sector Planner supports the Regional Flow Manager by validating sector constraints in the Sector Load Monitor and by advising whether demand smoothing is required before tactical execution.
The Slot Coordinator maintains accountability for Calculated Takeoff Time allocation policy and confirms that the Slot Allocation Engine applies the current Business Rules Registry parameters.
The Airline Operations Coordinator represents carrier operating priorities and confirms that Flight Intent Message updates are complete, timely, and traceable.

The Aircraft Operator Representative provides aircraft-specific constraints when requested and is responsible for ensuring that operator commitments entered in the Airport CDM Portal are operationally achievable.
The Network Operations Liaison coordinates with adjacent network units and confirms that regional measures remain compatible with upstream and downstream flow constraints.
The Network Operations Liaison also records external coordination outcomes in the Collaborative Decision Log so that later decisions can be reconstructed without relying on informal communications.
The Meteorology Briefing Officer produces the Storm Cell Snapshot before the pre-tactical capacity review begins.
The Meteorology Briefing Officer briefs forecast confidence, timing risk, and expected operational impact in the Digital Briefing Room using data supplied through the Weather Ingest Gateway.
When forecast uncertainty is material, the Meteorology Briefing Officer states the trigger conditions that would justify moving from Normal Operations to Adverse Weather Mode.

The Airport Duty Manager is the primary airport escalation contact and confirms that airport-side constraints are reflected consistently across the Airport CDM Portal and the Common Situation Display.
The Tower Supervisor is accountable for tactical runway sequencing decisions and confirms that the Tower Sequence Manager reflects the current runway configuration.
The Ramp Control Lead is accountable for apron movement coordination and maintains the Ramp Movement Board in a state that supports reliable departure metering.
The Ground Handling Dispatcher confirms that handling resource assumptions are current in the Handling Resource Planner and escalates material deviations through the Airport Duty Manager.
The Deicing Coordinator provides pre-tactical and tactical advice when winter operations affect departure readiness, metering stability, or achievable throughput.
The Military Airspace Liaison confirms military airspace availability assumptions and alerts the Regional Flow Manager when civil routing options may be constrained.

During tactical operations, the Regional Flow Manager chairs decision checkpoints and authorizes changes to flow measures when the Capacity Assessment Module indicates that declared capacity no longer matches observed conditions.
The Departure Metering Service and Arrival Regulation Console are used only under the authority of the accountable flow roles, and their outputs must remain visible on the Common Situation Display.

Escalation to the Emergency Response Coordinator is required when a safety event, security event, or emergency response activity may affect airport acceptance, surface movement, or airspace availability.
The System Support Engineer is the technical escalation contact for degraded Regional Flow Platform functions, interface outages, or abnormal behavior in the Flight Data Exchange.

The Data Governance Steward verifies that operational decisions, role acknowledgements, and exception handling are captured in the Audit Event Ledger with synchronized timestamps from the Time Synchronization Service.

At the end of each tactical period, accountable roles confirm that decisions and unresolved issues are available to the Performance Analytics Warehouse for later inclusion in the Post Operations Report.
